paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For most of the last century, the clock on the old mill in Ashby was the only public clock in the village. It was never accurate. Farmers joked that it showed the right time only twice a day, and most people preferred to listen for the bakery whistle instead.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: In 1987 a retired engineer, Mara Lind, offered to repair the mechanism without payment. She spent forty evenings in the mill tower, replacing worn gears with parts she made at home. When she finished, the clock lost less than a minute a month.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The repair changed village habits in small ways. The weekly market began to open at a fixed hour, and the school stopped ringing its own bell. Not everyone was pleased: the baker complained that nobody listened for his whistle any more.
